text: The QA workflow has 4 blocks executed in strict order: Knowledge Base -> Discovery -> Quality -> Release. Each block requires an explicit gate token from the user before the next block can proceed. The gate tokens are: KB_APPROVED, DISCOVERY_APPROVED, QUALITY_APPROVED, APPROVE_FOR_JIRA.

Jira connectivity check occurs at Release block start only. Knowledge Base, Discovery, and Quality blocks operate independently of Jira connectivity. If Jira MCP health check fails at Release block start, return a blocking error with a clear message.
Never publish to Jira unless the exact gate token APPROVE_FOR_JIRA is explicitly provided by the user. This is an absolute gate that cannot be bypassed under any circumstance.

Communication logging is mandatory. For each agent handoff, append one JSON line to agent_bus.jsonl with fields: ts (ISO8601), ticket (storyKey), from (agent), to (agent or conductor), block (Knowledge Base|Discovery|Quality|Release), status (PASSED|FAILED|WAITING_APPROVAL|RUNNING|NOT_STARTED|SKIPPED), message (summary), payload_ref (file path), errors (array).

The project serves two business domains determined by Jira sprint field: If sprint starts with 'PFPT', the domain is FOF (Fund of Funds) with target folder FOF/. If sprint starts with 'PFPM', the domain is Private Markets with target folder Private_Markets/. If sprint field is missing or blank, the domain cannot be assumed and must be classified by the conductor-agent.

Knowledge sources have a strict priority hierarchy: 1) Jira (Primary) - epics, stories, comments, linked issues, attachments, custom fields. 2) Uploaded Artifacts (Secondary) - domain folder files, design docs, architecture diagrams. 3) Confluence (Tertiary) - related pages, historical context. Public web search and external websites must never be used.

The PULSE project uses Jira with Xray for test management. Story keys follow the pattern PULSE-XXXX (e.g., PULSE-3730, PULSE-3739, PULSE-3892). Test cases are created as Jira Test issues and linked to stories using the 'is tested by' link type.

Investment data involves two primary clients: Pantheon and BlackRock. Pantheon investment files use PNT column references and Deal_ID for row identification (e.g., Deal_ID = 2280). BlackRock investment files use BLK column references. When both BLK and PNT columns are present in a scenario matrix, prefer the client-specific column that matches the uploaded source file.

Data quality testing involves scenario patterns such as: valid happy path with limited rows, only Contribution or Distribution rows with no POSITION_ID, mixed POSITION_ID (some null, some with values), and mixed Contribution and Distribution plus mixed POSITION_ID.

Jira Testing Type field supports exactly 5 values: Functional, Non Functional, Regression, End to End, Negative. All other testing types must be normalized: Data Validation -> Functional, Filtering -> Functional, Configuration -> Functional, Metadata -> Functional, Parametrization -> Functional, Execution -> Functional, Audit & Logging -> Functional, Performance -> Non Functional, Load Testing -> Non Functional, Stress Testing -> Non Functional, Integration -> End to End, Error Handling -> Negative, Input Validation -> Functional (or Negative if error-focused), Boundary -> Functional (or Negative). Default for unmatched values: Functional.

CSV to Jira field mapping: Test Case ID -> __xray_testId, Test Type -> xray_testtype, Testing Type -> customfield_10302, Assignee Name -> __assignee_name, Summary -> summary, Step Action -> __xray_step_action, Step Result -> __xray_step_result, Expected result -> __xray_step_result, Priority -> __priority_name, Story -> __issuelink_outward_10007, Data -> __step_data.
Testing Type label normalization: Use exact value 'End to end' (not 'End-to-End'). Convert all variants (End to End, End-to-End, Integration) to 'End to end' in generated outputs.

Standard test case template requires: Test Case ID (format: TC_<STORY>_NNN), Summary, Assignee Name, Description, Priority (Critical|High|Medium|Low), Test Component (UI|API|Backend|DataComparison), Testing Type (Functional|Non Functional|Regression|End to end|Negative), Pre-Requisites (array), Data (array), Steps (array of {Step No, Action, Expected Result}), Final Expected Result, Story (story key).

CSV export uses PULSE-3336 format. Columns: Test Scenario, Test Case ID, Test Type, Testing Type, Assignee Name, Summary, Data, Step Action, Expected result, Priority, Story. First row of each test case has all metadata + first step. Subsequent rows have metadata columns blank, only Step Action + Expected result. Blank row between different test cases. Test Scenario = Test Component. Test Type = always 'Manual' (or 'Automated' if applicable). Data = comma-separated key-value pairs.

Knowledge base document format: # [Epic/Story Key] - Knowledge Base, ## Summary, ## Business Context, ## Key Requirements, ## Acceptance Criteria, ## Important Decisions, ## Dependencies, ## Test Knowledge, ## Technical Notes, ## Risks, ## Open Questions, ## References (Jira, Confluence, Repository/docs, Attachments).

Mandatory test coverage categories: UI, API, Backend, DataComparison. Every story must have at least one test case for each category. If a category has no supporting acceptance criteria, create a coverage placeholder test case clearly marked as needing verification.

Test case types to include for every story: Functional/positive, Negative, Boundary, Integration, Regression. Each type should map to specific acceptance criteria. Do not include a test type if no supporting AC exists for it.

Testing techniques available: BVA (Boundary Value Analysis), ECP (Equivalence Class Partitioning), Decision Table, Negative testing, Integration testing, Regression scope. Each selected technique must map to at least one acceptance criterion. Do not select techniques the story cannot support.

Test data scenario classes to cover when relevant: Positive, Negative, Boundary, Null or empty, Format validation, Business-rule validation, Data-quality validation. For boundary scenarios, use: exact minimum, exact maximum, minimum minus 1, maximum plus 1, empty string, null.

Jira Cloud Subtask Access Bug: Direct API reads of sub-tasks sometimes return HTTP 404 despite the sub-task key appearing in the parent issue payload. Affected keys include PULSE-3892, PULSE-3740, PULSE-3800, PULSE-3901. Workaround: Extract sub-task metadata from parent issue's fields.subtasks array. For assignee resolution: 1) Attempt direct read with 3 retries + exponential backoff, 2) If all fail, extract from parent.fields.subtasks[], 3) Fall back to parent story assignee, 4) Log the failure.

Assignee resolution for test cases: Resolve from the Jira sub-task whose summary contains 'Test case design' linked to the story. Call mcp_io_statestree_jira_getIssue on the sub-task key. If no such sub-task exists, fall back to the parent story's assignee field. If all resolution fails, use 'UNRESOLVED' as the Assignee Name and log the failure.

Idempotent Jira publishing: Re-running the publish agent for the same story must not create duplicate test cases, must not create duplicate links, and must not add duplicate test runs to execution. Before creating a Jira Test issue, always search for an existing matching test first.

Acceptance criteria must be preserved verbatim from Jira. Do not rephrase, merge, split, or summarize AC items. Each AC becomes its own entry with a sequential ID (AC1, AC2, etc.) and a source_ref pointing back to the Jira story.

Completeness score calculation: Start at 100, deduct for gaps. No acceptance criteria: -20. No user artifacts: -15. Each empty resolvedContext category (businessRules, dependencies, environments, dataExpectations): -10. Each open question: -5. Each unresolved assumption: -3. Minimum score: 0.

Facts must be labeled with source attribution: [FACT - source: JIRA/<ticket-key>] for Jira data, [FACT - source: Artifact/<filename>] for uploaded files, [FACT - source: Confluence/<page-title>] for Confluence data, [ASSUMPTION] for anything inferred but not explicitly stated.

File output paths per storyKey: <DOMAIN>/<storyKey>_knowledge_base.md, runs/<storyKey>/discovery_context.json, runs/<storyKey>/quality_pack.json, runs/<storyKey>/<storyKey>_testcases.csv, runs/<storyKey>/review_pack.md, runs/<storyKey>/publish_report.json, runs/<storyKey>/agent_bus.jsonl, runs/<storyKey>/status_dashboard.md.

Source file safety: The original uploaded source file is immutable. Always create a new output file. Never overwrite the uploaded source file. Never rename, delete, or alter the original source artifact. Generated scenario files go under runs/<storyKey>/generated_test_data/. Do not write generated files back into original artifact directories.

Duplicate detection in test review: Compare test cases by their Steps and Expected Results, not just by Summary. Two test cases with different steps are not duplicates even if their summaries are similar.

discovery_context.json schema: story (embedded StoryAgent JSON), selectedTechniques (array), coverageTargets (array of UI/API/Backend/DataComparison), artifactInsights (array of {insight, source_ref}), resolvedContext ({businessRules, dependencies, environments, dataExpectations} - all arrays), assumptions (array of {text, approved}), openQuestions (array), completenessScore (0-100), gate ({requiredToken, status}).

quality_pack.json schema: storyKey, templateName, testCases (array of test case objects), traceability (array), coverageMatrix ({UI: bool, API: bool, Backend: bool, DataComparison: bool}), reviewSummary ({issuesFound, issuesResolved, openRisks}), gate ({requiredToken: QUALITY_APPROVED, status}).

StoryAgent output schema: key (storyKey), summary, description, acceptanceCriteria (array of {id, text, source_ref}), labels (array), attachments (array), completenessGaps (array of gap descriptions).

Pre-Requisites in test cases must be specific and unambiguous: specify which user role, which environment, what prior data state is required, and what page/screen the tester should be on. Do not use vague pre-requisites like 'User is logged in.'

Every test case step must be independently verifiable. Do not combine multiple actions and validations into one vague step. Each step must have its own Expected Result. Shorthand test cases with only a summary and a single Final Expected Result without granular steps must be rejected.

Publish report integrity: totalTestCases must equal created + reused + skipped + failed. Every test case from quality_pack.json must appear in the details array. No test case may be silently omitted. The jiraKey field must contain the actual key returned by the API, or null if creation failed.
